body.text: Who is a candidate for trifocal intraocular lenses vs LASIK?

LASIK reshapes the cornea and works best for younger adults whose natural eye lens still flexes cleanly for near reading. Once presbyopia stiffens the lens after age 45—or early cataracts begin clouding vision—refractive lens exchange (RLE) or cataract surgery with a trifocal intraocular lens (IOL) addresses both distance and near focus permanently.

An [American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) Ophthalmic Technology Assessment](https://www.aao.org/education/ophthalmic-technology-assessment/multifocal-accommodating-intraocular-lenses-treatm) confirms that presbyopia-correcting IOLs improve both distance and near visual acuity after lens removal. However, surgeons must verify healthy macula, retina, and tear-film status via optical coherence tomography (OCT) and biometry before approving trifocal optics, since night-driving halos and glare require honest pre-op counseling.
Are both eyes done on the same day or 24–48 hours apart?

Most international ophthalmic surgeons in Istanbul perform delayed sequential surgery—operating on the first eye on Day 2 and the second eye 24 to 48 hours later—rather than both eyes during a single sitting. Spacing the eyes allows a slit-lamp check of the first eye's healing and refractive target before proceeding.

Research reviewed by [AAO EyeNet on sequential bilateral cataract surgery](https://www.aao.org/eyenet/article/update-on-sequential-bilateral-cataract-surgery) and [AAO's 2026 immediate sequential bilateral safety review](https://www.aao.org/eyenet/article/isbcs-safety-and-evidence-part-1) notes that while same-day bilateral surgery is feasible under strict separate-sterilization protocols, delayed spacing remains standard to reduce bilateral infection risk and refine second-eye lens power. Your ophthalmologist sets the exact interval after measuring both eyes in person.

body.text: Which CE/FDA-approved lens brands should be documented in your discharge file?

Before signing surgical consent for lens replacement in Türkiye, confirm the exact manufacturer, optical model, and toric astigmatism specification your surgeon plans to implant. Reputable Istanbul eye hospitals stock globally traceable CE-marked and FDA-approved lenses and attach each lens's factory barcode sticker directly to your discharge card.

Well-documented presbyopia-correcting platforms include the FDA-approved [Alcon AcrySof IQ PanOptix trifocal IOL](https://www.alcon.com/media-release/alcon-introduces-acrysof-iq-panoptix-trifocal-iol-us-first-and-only-fda-approved/), the CE-marked [ZEISS AT LISA tri family](https://www.zeiss.com/meditec/en/products/intraocular-lenses-iols/trifocal-iols/at-lisa-tri-family.html), and the FDA-approved [Johnson & Johnson TECNIS Synergy IOL](https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/recently-approved-devices/tecnis-synergytm-intraocular-lens-iol-model-zfr00v-tecnis-synergytm-toric-ii-iol-models-zfw150). Always verify that your discharge file contains the following items before flying home:

items: Official IOL implant identification card with manufacturer name, model code, diopter power, and serial barcode for each eye
English operative report signed by the performing ophthalmologist
Pre-operative optical biometry and macular OCT scan printouts or digital files
Written antibiotic, steroid, and lubricating eye-drop schedule with tapering dates

body.text: How many days should you stay in Istanbul?

Plan five to six full nights in Istanbul for bilateral trifocal lens replacement or cataract surgery spaced 24 to 48 hours apart. This schedule covers Day 1 dilated biometry and retina scans, both surgical mornings, mandatory next-day pressure and slit-lamp checks after each eye, and one quiet buffer day before your return flight.

faq.q: Will I need cataract surgery later if I have refractive lens exchange now?
faq.a: No. Because refractive lens exchange replaces your natural crystalline lens with an artificial intraocular lens, cataracts cannot form on the implanted lens later in life.

faq.q: Are night-time halos normal after trifocal IOL implantation?
faq.a: Mild halos or rings around headlights are common during the first weeks to months as your brain adapts to multifocal optics. Discuss your night-driving needs openly with your surgeon during biometry testing.

faq.q: Can I fly home the day after my second eye surgery?
faq.a: Wait until your ophthalmologist completes the post-operative intraocular pressure and slit-lamp examination on the second eye and gives written clearance to fly, usually 24 to 48 hours later.

faq.q: Should I bring a travel companion to Istanbul for lens replacement?
faq.a: Yes. Dilating drops, temporary light sensitivity, and alternating eye shields make having a companion—or pre-arranged private driver transfers—far more comfortable between hotel and hospital visits.
